q.s: A 24-year-old woman has recurrent painful, shallow oral ulcers with a yellowish base, plus chronic diarrhea, iron deficiency anemia and an itchy blistering rash on her elbows. Which condition is most likely associated with her oral lesions?
e: Wrong. White patch, not painful ulcers.
Wrong. Vesicles on the lips that crust, not aphthae with diarrhea and rash.
Correct. Recurrent aphthous stomatitis is associated with celiac disease (dermatitis herpetiformis, iron deficiency), IBD, SLE, Behçet syndrome and HIV.

q.s: A 64-year-old man who smokes and drinks heavily has a nonhealing ulcer with raised, irregular borders on the lateral tongue. What is the most likely diagnosis?
e: Correct. The most common oral malignancy; associated with tobacco, alcohol and HPV-16.

q.s: Which oral lesions are precursors of squamous cell carcinoma?
A 45-year-old man has recurrent painful swelling under his jaw just before and during meals. Which condition is most likely?
e: Correct. A stone in a salivary duct causes peri-prandial pain and swelling; submandibular is common.

q.s: Risk factors for sialolithiasis include:
o: Salivary stasis such as dehydration, and trauma

q.s: A 52-year-old woman has a slowly growing painless mass in front of her ear. Excision shows epithelial cells in a chondromyxoid stroma. The tumor recurs years later. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. The most common salivary tumor; recurs if incompletely excised or ruptured.

q.s: A 65-year-old man who smokes has bilateral parotid masses. Histology shows cystic spaces lined by oncocytic epithelium with dense lymphoid stroma containing germinal centers. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Papillary cystadenoma lymphomatosum: benign, may be bilateral, linked to smoking.

q.s: What is the most common malignant salivary gland tumor?
e: Wrong. Not the most common per First Aid.

q.s: A parotid mass is accompanied by facial nerve paralysis. What does this suggest?
e: Wrong. Benign tumors rarely cause nerve palsy.
Correct. Facial paralysis or pain suggests malignancy.

q.s: Which salivary gland location makes a tumor more likely to be malignant?
e: Wrong. Most parotid tumors are benign.
Correct. Smaller glands harbor proportionally more malignant tumors.

q.s: Sialadenitis can be caused by which of the following?
o: Obstruction, infection (S. aureus, mumps) or immune-mediated disease (Sjögren)

q.s: A 38-year-old woman has progressive dysphagia to both solids and liquids for 2 years, regurgitation of undigested food and weight loss. Barium swallow shows a dilated esophagus tapering to a "bird's beak." Mechanism?
o: Loss of inhibitory NO- and VIP-containing neurons in the myenteric plexus, so the LES fails to relax

q.s: Which manometry findings are characteristic of achalasia?
o: Absent or uncoordinated peristalsis with elevated LES resting pressure and incomplete relaxation
Normal peristalsis with low LES pressure
Low LES pressure with absent distal peristalsis
Corkscrew contractions with normal LES pressure

q.s: A man from rural Brazil has achalasia and dilated cardiomyopathy. Which organism causes secondary achalasia here?
e: Correct. Chagas disease destroys myenteric neurons.

q.s: Achalasia increases the risk of which complication?
Dysphagia to both solids and liquids from the start suggests a motility disorder. Dysphagia mainly to solids, progressing later to liquids, suggests:
o: Mechanical obstruction such as cancer or stricture

q.s: Which treatment option for achalasia uses a toxin injected endoscopically?
e: Correct. Blocks ACh release, reducing LES tone.

q.s: An older adult develops achalasia-like dysphagia with rapid weight loss. Which secondary cause must be excluded?
Which nerve plexus degenerates in achalasia?
Warthin tumor is typically found in which group?
A 40-year-old man has heartburn after meals and at night, a chronic cough and hoarseness. Which mechanism underlies his condition?
o: Transient relaxations or decreased LES tone allowing reflux
e: Correct. GERD can present with cough and hoarseness (laryngopharyngeal reflux) and is associated with asthma.

q.s: A 70-year-old woman takes alendronate at bedtime without water. She now has severe pain on swallowing. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Bisphosphonates, tetracyclines, NSAIDs, ferrous sulfate and KCl cause pill esophagitis.

q.s: A 22-year-old man with asthma and allergic rhinitis has recurrent food impaction. Endoscopy shows concentric rings and linear furrows. Biopsy shows many eosinophils. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. Not the classic endoscopic finding.
Wrong. Linear ulcers in the immunosuppressed.

q.s: A man with AIDS (CD4 40/mm³) has odynophagia. Endoscopy shows white pseudomembranes that scrape off. Most likely cause?
e: Correct. The most common infectious esophagitis.

q.s: An immunosuppressed transplant patient has odynophagia. Endoscopy shows large linear ulcers. Biopsy shows enlarged cells with intranuclear inclusions. Organism?
A 45-year-old woman has dysphagia, iron deficiency anemia and glossitis. Barium swallow shows an upper esophageal web. Which cancer is she at increased risk for?
After a night of binge drinking and repeated vomiting, a 30-year-old man vomits bright red blood. He is hemodynamically stable with no crepitus. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Partial-thickness mucosal tears at the GE junction.
Wrong. Less likely with this history.

q.s: A 50-year-old man has severe chest pain and shortness of breath after violent retching. Crepitus is felt in the neck, and chest radiography shows pneumomediastinum. Diagnosis?
What is the most common cause of esophageal perforation?
A 50-year-old woman has intermittent dysphagia and chest pain mimicking angina. Barium swallow shows a "corkscrew" esophagus; LES pressure is normal. Which treatment helps?
A woman with limited scleroderma has severe reflux. Why?
o: Smooth muscle atrophy and fibrosis lower LES pressure and impair distal peristalsis

q.s: A biopsy from the distal esophagus of a man with long-standing GERD shows columnar epithelium with goblet cells. What is this change?
Barrett esophagus increases the risk of which cancer?
A 62-year-old obese man with chronic GERD has progressive dysphagia to solids and weight loss. Endoscopy shows a mass in the lower third of the esophagus. Most likely histology?
e: Correct. Lower 1/3; GERD, Barrett, obesity, smoking.

q.s: Which is a risk factor for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma?
o: Very hot liquids, alcohol and smoking
e: Correct. Also caustic strictures, achalasia, nitrosamines.

q.s: Why does esophageal cancer spread rapidly?
o: The esophageal wall lacks a serosa
It is always metastatic at onset

q.s: Esophageal varices are located in which part of the esophagus?
e: Correct. Dilated submucosal veins from portal hypertension.

q.s: Which esophageal cancer type is more common worldwide?
Complications of GERD include all of the following EXCEPT:
e: Correct. Achalasia is a primary motility disorder, not a GERD complication.

q.s: HSV-1 esophagitis characteristically shows which endoscopic finding?

rounds.t: Gastritis, Ménétrier disease, and gastric cancer

q.s: A 58-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis takes naproxen daily and now has epigastric pain and melena. Endoscopy shows multiple gastric erosions. Mechanism?
o: Reduced prostaglandin E2, decreasing mucosal protection

q.s: A patient in the ICU with 50% body surface area burns develops gastric ulcers. Mechanism?
A patient with a severe traumatic brain injury develops a gastric ulcer. Mechanism?
o: Increased vagal stimulation raising ACh and acid secretion (Cushing ulcer)

q.s: What is the most common cause of chronic gastritis, and where does it start?
o: H. pylori; antrum first, spreading to the body

q.s: Chronic H. pylori gastritis increases the risk of which lymphoma?
A 60-year-old woman with vitiligo has macrocytic anemia. Gastric biopsy shows atrophy of the body and fundus with sparing of the antrum. Antibodies target which structure?
o: H+/K+-ATPase of parietal cells and intrinsic factor

q.s: Chronic atrophic gastritis increases risk of gastric cancer through which sequence?
o: Atrophy → hypochlorhydria → hypergastrinemia and intestinal metaplasia

q.s: A 55-year-old man has weight loss, anorexia, vomiting, epigastric pain and leg edema. Endoscopy shows giant, brain-like gastric folds in the body and fundus with antral sparing. Serum albumin is low. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. Thick leathery wall from signet ring carcinoma.
Wrong. High acid, not protein loss.
Correct. Foveolar hyperplasia, protein loss and decreased acid ("WAVEE").

q.s: Ménétrier disease causes edema because of:
o: Protein loss from excess mucus production

q.s: A 48-year-old woman has early satiety and weight loss. Gastric biopsy shows mucin-filled cells with peripheral nuclei infiltrating a thickened, leathery stomach wall. Which mutation is commonly responsible?
e: Correct. Diffuse gastric cancer with signet ring cells (linitis plastica).

q.s: Intestinal-type gastric adenocarcinoma is associated with which factors?
o: H. pylori, dietary nitrosamines, smoking, achlorhydria and chronic gastritis

q.s: A patient with gastric cancer has a palpable left supraclavicular lymph node. What is it called?
A woman has bilateral ovarian masses composed of mucin-secreting signet ring cells. Where is the primary tumor most likely located?
e: Wrong. Bilateral signet ring tumors are metastatic.

q.s: A firm periumbilical subcutaneous nodule in a patient with gastric cancer is called:
On rectal examination of a patient with gastric cancer, a firm mass is felt anteriorly in the rectouterine pouch. This is called:
A patient develops sudden eruption of multiple seborrheic keratoses. Which malignancy should be considered?
Gastrointestinal stromal tumors commonly carry mutations in which genes?
Intestinal-type gastric cancer most commonly appears where and how?
o: In the fundus as a submucosal mass
Diffusely, as a thick leathery stomach
On the lesser curvature, as an ulcer with raised margins
On the greater curvature as a polyp

q.s: Which skin finding can accompany gastric cancer as a paraneoplastic sign in the "WEAPON" mnemonic?
Autoimmune gastritis affects which region of the stomach?

rounds.t: Peptic ulcer disease, complications, GI bleeding

q.s: A 45-year-old man has epigastric pain that improves with eating and has gained weight. Which statement about his likely ulcer is correct?
o: About 90% are associated with H. pylori, and they are not routinely biopsied
It is caused by decreased acid secretion
e: Wrong. Duodenal ulcers are generally benign.

q.s: A 62-year-old woman has epigastric pain worse with meals and weight loss. Endoscopy shows a gastric ulcer. What should be done?
o: Biopsy the ulcer margins to rule out malignancy
e: Wrong. Gastric ulcers should be biopsied.
Correct. Gastric ulcers carry a higher risk of carcinoma.

q.s: Which condition causes duodenal ulcers through acid hypersecretion?
What is the most common complication of peptic ulcer disease?
A gastric ulcer on the lesser curvature bleeds massively. Which artery is most likely involved?
e: Wrong. Posterior stomach into the lesser sac.

q.s: An ulcer on the posterior wall of the first part of the duodenum bleeds. Which artery?
A 40-year-old man with a history of duodenal ulcer has sudden severe abdominal pain radiating to the right shoulder. Upright chest radiography shows air under the diaphragm. Where was the ulcer?
e: Correct. Anterior ulcers perforate into the peritoneal cavity (pneumoperitoneum); shoulder pain via phrenic nerve irritation.

q.s: Why is the pain of a perforated ulcer referred to the shoulder?
o: Irritation of the diaphragm innervated by the phrenic nerve (C3–C5)

q.s: An ulcer on the posterior gastric wall erodes into the lesser sac and bleeds from which artery?
e: Correct (per First Aid); splenic branches can also be involved.

q.s: Upper GI bleeding is defined as bleeding proximal to which landmark?
Upper GI bleeding typically presents with:
o: Bright red blood per rectum only

q.s: Which is a cause of lower GI bleeding?
e: Correct. Also angiodysplasia, IBD, hemorrhoids, fissure, cancer.

q.s: Gastric ulcers are associated with H. pylori in about what percentage of cases?
The main mechanism of gastric ulcer formation is:
Ulcers causing gastric outlet obstruction are most often located where?
Which duodenal ulcer location more commonly bleeds?
NSAIDs are a classic additional cause of which ulcer type?
e: Wrong. First Aid lists Zollinger-Ellison for duodenal.

q.s: A patient with melena has a negative upper endoscopy and colonoscopy. Melena still indicates bleeding mostly from which location?
o: Proximal to the ligament of Treitz or the small bowel
e: Correct. Melena results from digested blood, usually upper GI.

q.s: Hematochezia in an older adult with no pain is most commonly due to which listed cause?
Which statement best compares gastric and duodenal ulcer pain?
o: Gastric ulcer pain can worsen with meals (weight loss); duodenal ulcer pain improves with meals (weight gain)

q.s: A 28-year-old woman has chronic diarrhea, bloating, iron deficiency anemia and an itchy vesicular rash on her elbows and knees. Duodenal biopsy shows villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia and intraepithelial lymphocytes. Which serologic test is the best initial screen?
o: IgA anti-tissue transglutaminase with total IgA
e: Correct. Celiac disease; check total IgA because selective IgA deficiency causes false negatives.

q.s: Celiac disease is associated with which HLA types?
e: Correct. "I ate (8) too (2) much gluten at Dairy Queen."

q.s: Celiac disease primarily affects which part of the bowel?
A patient with celiac disease who continues to eat gluten develops weight loss and abdominal pain years later. Which malignancy is increased?
Which skin condition is associated with celiac disease?
A patient with suspected celiac disease has selective IgA deficiency. Which testing approach avoids a false negative?
o: IgG-based tests (eg, IgG deamidated gliadin peptide)

q.s: A 20-year-old man has bloating, flatulence and diarrhea after drinking milk. Biopsy shows normal villi. A hydrogen breath test rises >20 ppm after lactose. What happens to stool pH?
o: It rises because of bicarbonate secretion
It decreases because colonic bacteria ferment lactose
e: Correct. Osmotic diarrhea with acidic stool.

q.s: A child develops lactose intolerance after a viral gastroenteritis. Why?
o: Injury to the villous tips where lactase is located

q.s: A 40-year-old man with chronic alcohol use has steatorrhea and weight loss. D-xylose absorption is normal, and fecal elastase is low. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Malabsorption of fat, fat-soluble vitamins and B12 with normal mucosal absorption.

q.s: Why can pancreatic insufficiency cause vitamin B12 deficiency?
o: Pancreatic proteases are needed to release B12 from R-binders so it can bind intrinsic factor
B12 is absorbed in the stomach

q.s: A volunteer returning from 6 months in South Asia has chronic diarrhea, malabsorption and megaloblastic anemia from folate deficiency. Biopsy resembles celiac disease but symptoms improve with antibiotics and folate. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. Does not respond to antibiotics.

q.s: A 60-year-old man has arthralgias, memory problems and heart murmur, followed later by diarrhea and weight loss. Duodenal biopsy shows foamy macrophages in the lamina propria that stain PAS-positive. Organism?
e: Correct. Whipple disease: Cardiac, Arthralgias, Neurologic symptoms ("foamy Whipped cream in a CAN").

q.s: Which test screens for fat malabsorption?
In celiac disease, what is the D-xylose test result?
o: Normal in blood, low in urine only

q.s: Celiac disease is associated with reduced bone density because of:
o: Malabsorption of calcium and vitamin D
Excess PTH from a parathyroid adenoma

q.s: Which enzyme deamidates gliadin, making it more immunogenic in celiac disease?
e: Correct. Deamidated gliadin binds HLA-DQ2/8 on APCs.

q.s: The treatment of celiac disease is:
Pancreatic insufficiency causes which change in duodenal contents?
Whipple disease is most common in which group?
Tropical sprue affects which bowel segments and causes which anemia first?
o: Duodenum and jejunum (later ileum); megaloblastic anemia from folate deficiency, later B12

rounds.t: Inflammatory bowel disease, IBS, and appendicitis

q.s: A 24-year-old man has crampy right lower quadrant pain, nonbloody diarrhea and weight loss. Colonoscopy shows skip lesions with cobblestone mucosa in the terminal ileum and a normal rectum. Biopsy shows noncaseating granulomas. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. Continuous from the rectum, no granulomas.
Correct. Transmural, skip lesions, rectal sparing, granulomas.

q.s: A 30-year-old woman has bloody diarrhea with urgency. Colonoscopy shows continuous friable mucosa from the rectum to the splenic flexure with crypt abscesses; no granulomas. Which antibody is commonly positive?
A man with ulcerative colitis has fatigue, pruritus and elevated alkaline phosphatase. MRCP shows beading of intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts. Diagnosis?
A patient with Crohn disease has recurrent urinary tract infections and passes air in her urine. Which complication?
Why are patients with Crohn disease of the ileum prone to calcium oxalate kidney stones?
o: Malabsorbed fat binds calcium, leaving oxalate free to be absorbed

q.s: A patient with severe ulcerative colitis has fever, tachycardia and a markedly distended transverse colon (8 cm) on radiograph. Diagnosis?
Which radiographic finding is classic for long-standing ulcerative colitis?
o: "Lead pipe" colon from loss of haustra

q.s: Which drug class is a mainstay for mild to moderate ulcerative colitis?
Which extraintestinal manifestation is shared by both Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis?
o: Primary sclerosing cholangitis only in Crohn
e: Correct. Also uveitis, episcleritis, aphthous ulcers and arthritis.

q.s: Which stool test helps distinguish inflammatory bowel disease from irritable bowel syndrome?
A 68-year-old woman has chronic watery diarrhea for 6 months. Colonoscopy shows normal mucosa, but biopsy shows a thickened subepithelial collagen band. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Most common in older women.

q.s: A 35-year-old woman has recurrent abdominal pain related to defecation with alternating stool frequency for a year. Colonoscopy and labs are normal. She also has fibromyalgia and anxiety. What is the first-line treatment?
An 18-year-old has periumbilical pain that migrates to the right lower quadrant over 12 hours with fever and nausea. Why is the early pain periumbilical?
o: Distension stimulates visceral afferents entering at T8–T10
Somatic pain from the abdominal wall
The appendix is located at the umbilicus
e: Correct. Visceral pain is poorly localized; localized RLQ pain follows parietal peritoneum irritation.

q.s: What commonly obstructs the appendix in children?
Pressing on the left lower quadrant causes pain in the right lower quadrant. What is this sign?
McBurney point is located:
o: One-third of the distance from the right ASIS to the umbilicus
Two-thirds from the umbilicus to the ASIS
Midway between the umbilicus and pubis
e: Wrong. Equivalent but phrased differently; the standard description is 1/3 from the ASIS.

q.s: Which feature distinguishes Crohn disease histology from ulcerative colitis?
Colorectal cancer risk in ulcerative colitis rises with:
Which antibiotic is used in Crohn disease, particularly for perianal disease?
Ulcerative colitis inflammation involves which layers?

rounds.t: Diverticula, Hirschsprung disease, malrotation, intussusception, volvulus

q.s: A 72-year-old man has sudden painless passage of a large amount of bright red blood per rectum. He has a low-fiber diet. Colonoscopy later shows many sigmoid outpouchings. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. Right colon, also painless, but diverticula seen.

q.s: Colonic diverticula are classified as false diverticula because they:
o: Contain all layers of the bowel wall
Contain only mucosa and submucosa herniating at weak points where vasa recta penetrate

q.s: A 65-year-old woman has left lower quadrant pain, fever and leukocytosis. CT shows sigmoid wall thickening with inflamed diverticula. Later she notices air bubbles in her urine. Which complication?
A 75-year-old man has dysphagia, gurgling, regurgitation of undigested food and foul breath. A neck mass appears after meals. Where is the defect?
o: Killian triangle, between the thyropharyngeal and cricopharyngeal parts of the inferior constrictor

q.s: A 2-year-old has painless rectal bleeding with dark red stool. A 99mTc-pertechnetate scan shows uptake in the right lower quadrant. What tissue takes up the tracer?
o: Ectopic acid-secreting gastric mucosa in a Meckel diverticulum
e: Wrong. Can be present but does not take up pertechnetate.

q.s: Meckel diverticulum is a persistence of which structure?
The "rule of 2's" for Meckel diverticulum includes:
o: 2 types of epithelium: squamous and transitional
2 feet from the ileocecal valve, 2 inches long, 2% of the population

q.s: A newborn with Down syndrome fails to pass meconium within 48 hours and has bilious vomiting and distension. Rectal exam causes explosive release of stool. Diagnosis is confirmed by:
o: Rectal suction biopsy showing absent ganglion cells

q.s: Hirschsprung disease results from failure of which process, and which gene is associated?
o: Neural crest cell migration; loss-of-function RET mutations

q.s: In Hirschsprung disease, which segment of bowel is dilated?
o: The normal bowel proximal to the aganglionic segment

q.s: A 3-week-old infant has sudden bilious vomiting. Upper GI series shows the duodenum failing to cross midline with a corkscrew pattern. Fibrous bands are found at surgery. What is the underlying anomaly?

A 9-month-old has episodes of severe colicky pain during which he draws his legs to his chest, vomiting and "currant jelly" stools. A sausage-shaped mass is felt in the right abdomen. Ultrasound shows a target sign. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Most commonly at the ileocecal junction.
Wrong. Can be a lead point.

q.s: In children, idiopathic intussusception is associated with which factor?
o: Recent viral infection (eg, adenovirus) or rotavirus vaccine causing Peyer patch hypertrophy

q.s: An adult develops intussusception. What is the most likely lead point?
An 80-year-old nursing home resident has abdominal distension and constipation. Radiograph shows a "coffee bean" sign. Diagnosis?
A woman with a paraesophageal hernia has severe epigastric pain, dry heaving and a nasogastric tube cannot be passed. Diagnosis?
After extensive ileal resection for Crohn disease, a patient has voluminous postprandial diarrhea, weight loss and kidney stones. Diagnosis?
Which diverticulum is a "true" diverticulum?
Diverticulosis is associated with which dietary pattern?
o: Low fiber, high total fat and red meat, plus obesity

q.s: Zenker diverticulum is most common in which group?

rounds.t: Vascular and other intestinal disorders, polyps, colorectal cancer

q.s: A 74-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation not on anticoagulation has sudden severe abdominal pain. The abdomen is soft with minimal tenderness. Lactate is elevated. Most likely diagnosis?
o: Acute mesenteric ischemia from SMA embolism
e: Correct. Pain out of proportion to examination.
Wrong. Crampy pain then bleeding, watershed areas.

q.s: A 70-year-old man with peripheral arterial disease has epigastric pain 30 minutes after eating, fear of food and a 10-kg weight loss. Which artery is most commonly affected?
e: Wrong. Can be involved but SMA is most common.

q.s: An 82-year-old man with aortic stenosis has recurrent painless hematochezia. Colonoscopy shows tortuous dilated vessels in the cecum. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Right colon; associated with ESRD, von Willebrand disease and aortic stenosis.

q.s: An elderly patient after cardiac surgery with hypotension has crampy left-sided abdominal pain followed by bloody diarrhea. CT shows "thumbprinting" at the splenic flexure. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. Small bowel, pain out of proportion.

q.s: After abdominal surgery and opioid use, a patient has abdominal distension, decreased bowel sounds and no flatus. Imaging shows diffuse bowel dilation without a transition zone. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Hypomotility without obstruction; associated with surgery, opiates, hypokalemia, sepsis.

q.s: A 3-week-old premature formula-fed infant has bloody stools and abdominal distension. Radiograph shows gas within the bowel wall. Diagnosis?
What is the most common cause of small bowel obstruction?
A patient after gastric bypass has bloating, chronic watery diarrhea and B12 deficiency. A carbohydrate breath test is positive. Diagnosis?
Which colonic polyp has the highest malignant potential?
Serrated polyps progress to cancer through which pathway?
o: CpG island methylation silencing MLH1 with microsatellite instability and BRAF mutations

q.s: A 16-year-old has thousands of colonic polyps carpeting the colon and rectum. His father died of colon cancer at 38. Which gene is mutated?
e: Correct. Familial adenomatous polyposis; prophylactic colectomy.

q.s: A patient with FAP also has osteomas of the mandible, supernumerary teeth and congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium. Which syndrome?
A 14-year-old has dark macules on her lips and buccal mucosa and recurrent intussusception from small bowel hamartomatous polyps. She is at increased risk for which cancers?
o: Breast and GI cancers (colorectal, stomach, small bowel, pancreas)

q.s: A 42-year-old woman has right-sided colon cancer. Her mother had endometrial cancer at 48 and an uncle had colon cancer at 45. Which genes are likely mutated?
e: Correct. Lynch syndrome: CEOSS (Colon, Endometrial, Ovarian, Stomach, Skin).

q.s: A patient with FAP develops a medulloblastoma. Which syndrome?
A 70-year-old man has fatigue and iron deficiency anemia without visible bleeding. Colonoscopy shows an exophytic cecal mass. Why do right-sided colon cancers typically present this way?
o: They bleed occultly into a wide lumen with liquid stool, so obstruction is late

q.s: When should an average-risk adult begin colorectal cancer screening?
A man's father was diagnosed with colon cancer at 52. When should the son start colonoscopy screening?
o: At age 40, or 10 years before the relative's age at diagnosis, whichever is earlier

q.s: What is CEA used for in colorectal cancer?
In the chromosomal instability pathway of colorectal cancer, what is the correct order of mutations?
o: APC loss → KRAS mutation → loss of TP53/DCC

rounds.t: Cirrhosis, portal hypertension, liver tests, and liver tumors

q.s: A 55-year-old man with alcohol-associated cirrhosis has gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, spider angiomas and palmar erythema. What causes these findings?
o: Increased estrogen from reduced hepatic metabolism

q.s: Ascitic fluid analysis in a patient with cirrhosis shows a serum-ascites albumin gradient of 1.8 g/dL. What does this indicate?
Besides cirrhosis, which infection is a classic cause of portal hypertension worldwide?
A 30-year-old woman with polycythemia vera has abdominal pain, tender hepatomegaly and new ascites. JVP is normal. Imaging shows thrombosis of the hepatic veins. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Hepatic venous outflow obstruction; no JVD.

q.s: A patient with cirrhosis and ascites has fever and worsening confusion. Paracentesis shows an ascitic neutrophil count of 480/mm³. What is the empiric treatment?
o: A third-generation cephalosporin such as ceftriaxone (or cefotaxime)
e: Correct. Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, usually E. coli or Klebsiella.

q.s: The diagnostic threshold for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis is ascitic fluid neutrophils above:
A 50-year-old man has AST 260 U/L and ALT 105 U/L. Which cause is suggested by this pattern?
A patient has ALP of 520 U/L. Which test helps determine whether it is from liver or bone?
e: Correct. Elevated in liver/biliary disease but not bone disease.

q.s: Which laboratory value best reflects the liver's synthetic function over days?
e: Correct. Clotting factors have short half-lives.

q.s: Aminotransferases above 1000 U/L suggest which group of causes?
o: Acetaminophen toxicity, ischemic hepatitis, acute viral or autoimmune hepatitis

q.s: A 7-year-old with varicella treated with aspirin develops vomiting, confusion and hepatomegaly. Glucose is low and ammonia is high. Mechanism?
o: Aspirin metabolites inhibit mitochondrial β-oxidation, causing microvesicular steatosis

q.s: In which pediatric condition is aspirin still used despite the risk of Reye syndrome?
A liver biopsy from a heavy drinker shows swollen hepatocytes with neutrophils and eosinophilic intracytoplasmic inclusions of damaged keratin. These inclusions are:
Why does alcohol cause fatty liver?
o: Excess NADH decreases fatty acid oxidation and increases lipogenesis

q.s: An obese woman with type 2 diabetes and hypertriglyceridemia has elevated ALT. Biopsy shows steatosis, hepatocyte ballooning and lobular inflammation without alcohol use. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Can progress to cirrhosis and HCC.

q.s: A 30-year-old woman has fatigue and ALT 480 U/L. Anti-smooth muscle antibodies are positive. Biopsy shows portal and periportal lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate. Diagnosis?
A patient with cirrhosis becomes confused with asterixis after an upper GI bleed. What drug increases conversion of ammonia to ammonium in the gut?
e: Wrong. Not the listed first line.
Correct. Acidifies the colon, trapping NH4+.

q.s: Which is a trigger of hepatic encephalopathy by increasing ammonia production?
A 38-year-old woman has an incidental liver mass with a central stellate scar on CT. She is asymptomatic. Diagnosis?
e: Wrong. Associated with OCPs; no central scar.

q.s: A 28-year-old woman taking oral contraceptives for 10 years presents with sudden right upper quadrant pain and hypotension. Imaging shows bleeding from a liver mass. Diagnosis?

rounds.t: Inherited liver disease, jaundice, biliary disease, gallstones, and pancreatitis

q.s: A 35-year-old nonsmoker has dyspnea from panacinar emphysema of the lower lobes and elevated liver enzymes. Liver biopsy shows PAS-positive globules in hepatocytes. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Misfolded protein accumulates in hepatocyte ER.

q.s: A breastfed 7-day-old has mild jaundice that began on day 3. Total bilirubin is 13 mg/dL, all unconjugated. The infant is feeding well. Which factor contributes to normal neonatal jaundice?
o: Immature UDP-glucuronosyltransferase activity and high RBC turnover
Hemolytic disease of the newborn only

q.s: How does phototherapy treat neonatal unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia?
o: It isomerizes unconjugated bilirubin to a water-soluble form excreted in bile

q.s: Breast milk jaundice is caused by which mechanism?
o: β-glucuronidase in breast milk deconjugating bilirubin and increasing enterohepatic circulation

q.s: A 4-week-old has persistent jaundice, dark urine, pale acholic stools and hepatomegaly. Direct bilirubin and GGT are elevated. Ultrasound shows an abnormal gallbladder. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Most common reason for pediatric liver transplant.

q.s: A 22-year-old college student has mild jaundice during exam week after skipping meals. Bilirubin is 3.1 mg/dL, mostly unconjugated, with normal CBC and liver enzymes. Diagnosis?
A newborn has severe unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia and kernicterus. Phenobarbital has no effect. Which enzyme defect?
A 25-year-old has mild conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and a grossly black liver on laparoscopy. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Defective excretion; dark liver from epinephrine metabolites.

q.s: A 19-year-old has tremor, dysarthria, mood changes and elevated liver enzymes. Slit-lamp exam shows golden-brown corneal rings. Serum ceruloplasmin is low. Which gene is mutated?
Which drugs treat Wilson disease?
o: Penicillamine or trientine, and oral zinc

q.s: A 52-year-old man has diabetes, bronze skin, arthritis of the 2nd and 3rd MCP joints and hepatomegaly. Ferritin and transferrin saturation are very high. Which gene and hormone are involved?
e: Correct. Hereditary hemochromatosis increases iron absorption.

q.s: A 50-year-old woman with Hashimoto thyroiditis has pruritus, fatigue and elevated ALP. Antimitochondrial antibodies are positive. What is the treatment?
Primary sclerosing cholangitis increases the risk of which malignancy?

A 42-year-old obese woman with four children has had several episodes of dull RUQ pain after fatty meals lasting 1–2 hours. Labs are normal; ultrasound shows gallstones. Which hormone triggers the pain?
e: Correct. Biliary colic from gallbladder contraction against a stone in the cystic duct.

q.s: Black pigment gallstones are associated with which condition?
o: Chronic hemolysis (eg, sickle cell disease) or alcohol-associated cirrhosis

q.s: A 70-year-old woman has small bowel obstruction. Radiograph shows air in the biliary tree and a calcified stone in the right iliac fossa. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Rigler triad; the stone obstructs the ileocecal valve via a cholecystoenteric fistula.

q.s: A 65-year-old man has fever, jaundice, RUQ pain, confusion and hypotension. Which syndrome is this, and what is the usual cause?
o: Reynolds pentad; biliary obstruction with infection (acute cholangitis)

q.s: A 45-year-old woman with gallstones has severe epigastric pain radiating to the back and lipase 8 times the upper limit. Which is the most likely cause, and which lab finding may complicate it?
o: Gallstone pancreatitis; hypocalcemia from calcium soap formation

q.s: Four weeks after acute pancreatitis, a patient has early satiety and a palpable epigastric mass. CT shows a fluid collection with a wall lined by granulation tissue. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Lined by granulation tissue, not epithelium.

q.s: A 66-year-old man who smokes has painless jaundice, weight loss, back pain and recurrent tender cords in the veins of his arms and legs. CA 19-9 is markedly elevated. Which genetic abnormality is most common in his likely tumor?
e: Correct. Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (head of pancreas; Trousseau migratory thrombophlebitis, Courvoisier sign).
